topic: Common swift (Apus apus): Hedenström et al., Current Biology 2016 — micro data loggers on swifts breeding in Sweden showed 10-month non-stop flight outside the breeding season, some individuals never landing in that time; they feed on aerial insects, drink by skimming, and sleep in short bouts during slow ascending glides at dusk and dawn; breeding season ~2 months on land; juveniles may remain airborne 2–3 years until first breeding; winter in sub-Saharan Africa, especially the Congo basin, tracking rain fronts.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: The albatross or the Arctic tern holds the record for staying in the air.
myths.reality: Albatrosses and terns cover vast distances but land on water or shore to rest; the common swift stays airborne for ten months without landing (Hedenström et al. 2016).

hedenstrom_2016.title: Annual 10-Month Aerial Life Phase in the Common Swift Apus apus — Hedenström, Norevik, Warfvinge, Andersson, Bäckman, Åkesson, Curr Biol 2016;26(22):3066–3070
hedenstrom_2016.notes: micro data loggers on 13 swifts from Sweden; birds airborne >99 % of the 10-month non-breeding period; three individuals never landed; brief roosting only in some birds

lund_news.title: Swifts spend ten months in the air
lund_news.notes: Lund University researchers; swifts breeding in southern Sweden; ten months without landing; feed, drink and presumably sleep in flight

britannica_swift.title: Swift — bird
britannica_swift.notes: Apus apus; feeds on aerial insects; drinks by skimming water; winters in Africa south of the Sahara; young may not land for two to three years

bto_swift.title: Swift — BirdFacts
bto_swift.notes: on land only during the roughly two-month breeding season; winters in the Congo basin and southern Africa; follows rain fronts rich in insects

rspb_swift.title: Swift
rspb_swift.notes: sleeps on the wing in slow ascending glides at dusk; young birds may stay airborne for two or three years
